speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and current symptoms, I need to assess the severity and progression of your vision loss. How long have you been experiencing the black spots and decreased vision in your right eye?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the presence of black spots (floaters) and painless vision loss in an AIDS patient, I am highly suspicious of CMV retinitis. REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages are classic for Cytomegalovirus retinitis. Do you have any history of prior ocular infections or current use of antiretroviral therapy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of painless vision loss with floaters, combined with the classic "cottage cheese and ketchup" appearance on fundoscopy in an AIDS patient, is diagnostic for Cytomegalovirus retinitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
